theoryOfChange: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) describes its strategic approach in its annual impact reports. The '2024 Impact Report' highlights the organization's 'People x Biology x Data' strategy as an 'innovative framework' that integrates bioinformatics, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning to advance cancer immunotherapy. This framework aims to enhance researchers' ability to analyze complex biological data, identify novel biomarkers, and develop personalized treatment strategies, thereby accelerating the pace of discovery and ensuring new insights are translated into effective therapies for patients. The report also refers to this as a 'cohesive strategy to advance cancer immunotherapy, turning bold ideas into real-world impact.'

It has earned the <cite id="11">Candid Platinum Seal of Transparency</cite>, the highest level available, by sharing comprehensive data on its goals and results. Financially, the organization is stable with <cite id="12">21.2 months of working capital</cite> in reserve, ensuring that long-term research projects are not interrupted by short-term market fluctuations. Its governance is supported by a large and diverse <cite id="13">board of 34 members</cite>, providing significant oversight for its <cite id="14">worldwide geographic coverage</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: founded in 1953, the Cancer Research Institute (CRI) is a global leader in advancing immunotherapy to treat all types of cancer. The organization focuses on funding <cite id="1">clinician-scientists launching innovative phase I/II clinical studies</cite> that utilize the body's immune system to fight disease. In FY2023, the charity reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $32,295,259</cite>, though it faced a significant <cite id="3">26% revenue decline</cite> moving into the following fiscal year. Despite this financial shift, CRI maintains a <cite id="4">94/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting strong accountability and leadership. The organization operates with high efficiency, spending only <cite id="5">$0.11 to raise every $1 in donations</cite>. While its mission is global, CRI's primary impact is systemic, driving long-term changes in cancer care through research grants. In 2023 alone, the institute <cite id="6">awarded 73 new research grants</cite> and managed <cite id="7">$28.7 million in new research funding</cite>. This funding supports a variety of programs, including the <cite id="8">CRI Lloyd J. Old STARs Program</cite> and various postdoctoral fellowships. By focusing on high-potential research that might otherwise lack funding, CRI aims to bring effective immunotherapies to more patient populations worldwide.
